tldr: PostHog's pure product analytics is genuinely weaker than Mixpanel's or Amplitude's, and complex reports push you into SQL. I still recommend it to most founders, because it bundles session replay, feature flags, experiments and a real data warehouse into one tool at a stage when standing those up separately costs more than the analytics depth you give up.
faq: For most founders, yes — despite its product analytics being weaker than Mixpanel's or Amplitude's. It bundles product analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments and a data warehouse in one place, which is worth more early than the analytics depth you trade away.
The depth. Building a complex report through the UI gets painful, and for anything genuinely deep you drop into SQL — which costs you time that Mixpanel or Amplitude wouldn't.
PostHog vs Mixpanel — which should I pick?

If you already have a warehouse, or you want the best pure product analytics and nothing else, pick Mixpanel. If you want the whole stack under one roof without standing up a warehouse separately, PostHog is hard to beat.
Is PostHog's data warehouse a real warehouse?

Real enough to matter. You can run SQL across your product events alongside external data it pulls in from Stripe, Google Ads, HubSpot and dozens of other sources — which Mixpanel and Amplitude simply don't offer.
When should you move off PostHog?
When the analytics depth starts costing you more than the bundling saves — when your team is writing SQL for questions a purpose-built product analytics tool would answer in a few clicks.
